correzioni: «Lo sapevi?»: the quote from Atkinson's hospital bed was embellished. folklore.org (Hertzfeld, «I Still Remember Regions») gives «Don't worry, Steve, I still remember regions», so it now reads «Non preoccuparti, Steve, mi ricordo ancora le regioni». Also added «grave» to the 1982 accident and fixed the punctuation.

Kay and the term «object-oriented»: the text stated it as certain («Nel 1967… rispose: programmazione orientata agli oggetti»). It now follows his e-mail to Stefan Ram of 23 July 2003: «Fu probabilmente nel 1967… rispose: «È programmazione orientata agli oggetti»».
Visual Basic: «il 20 maggio 1991» could not be confirmed (sources say May 1991 at Comdex/Windows World in Atlanta; one says 20 March). Changed to «nel maggio 1991» in the text and the tappe.

1968 demo: «ponti radio» and «una cinquantina di chilometri» were not confirmed. They now read «con un modem costruito dal suo gruppo e con collegamenti video» and «a più di quaranta chilometri» (Menlo Park to San Francisco is about 42 km in a straight line).

Xerox Alto: «progettato da Chuck Thacker con Butler Lampson» became «ideato da Butler Lampson e progettato soprattutto da Chuck Thacker» (Lampson's 1972 memo «Why Alto?»). Added that Bill English also moved to PARC.

Jobs at PARC: the vague «La Apple stava già lavorando a una macchina con interfaccia grafica» became the Lisa, an office computer, pushed toward windows and mouse by the visit. Added the deal (100.000 azioni per circa un milione di dollari). Goldberg «si rifiutò… temendo che la Apple se ne appropriasse», following CHM's wording.
Objects were not «invented» for graphical interfaces (Simula was made for simulation). The sentence now says «il genere di problema in cui gli oggetti danno il meglio».

Smalltalk's name: brought the paraphrase in line with Kay's «The Early History of Smalltalk» (Zeus, Odin, Thor; an innocuous label, people pleasantly surprised) and explained «Smalltalk» = «chiacchiere». Byte: «quasi un intero numero» became «un numero speciale»; *Byte* is now in italics in the text and the tappe.

Mouse: «si rivelò la più comoda» became «Nelle prove finanziate dalla NASA, a confronto con penne ottiche e joystick, risultò la più efficace». The potentiometer is now explained as a variable resistor that turns rotation into a voltage (the link to electronics). Engelbart in protagonisti: «Inventa il mouse con Bill English».

Mac: added that about a third of the 64 KB ROM was QuickDraw, written in 68000 assembly (Byte 1984 and the CHM source-code release). Atkinson in protagonisti: «QuickDraw, la grafica del Lisa e del Macintosh, e MacPaint».

HyperCard and the wiki: the first wiki now comes from a HyperCard stack Cunningham built in the late 1980s, and the design-patterns paragraph adds that the wiki (March 1995) was opened to discuss patterns. Myst is now in italics and «copione» is glossed as *script*.

Eiffel: «ogni metodo dichiara» became «può dichiarare» a contract. Visual Basic now links {{BASIC}} (glossary term owned by chapter personal). Christopher Alexander now has his book (*A Pattern Language*, 1977). «L'anno dopo arriverà Java» became «Nello stesso anno», to follow the 1995 wiki.

Italian: block «Stampi, esemplari e messaggi» mixed present and past tense; it is now in past tense like the rest of the chapter. Also «istruzioni che lavorano» became «lavoravano», the paragraph now names {{incapsulamento}} where the idea first appears, and «GUI, *graphical user interface*» is in italics.

Fonti: replaced six links I could not confirm. Krogdahl's PDF at an uncertain UiO path became the original Dahl and Nygaard paper, «Class and Subclass Declarations» (Buxton, North-Holland 1968, pp. 158–174). A CHM Revolution page with an unknown id became Sutherland's thesis (Cambridge UCAM-CL-TR-574). The 1968 IEEE milestone, which may not exist, became the IEEE Milestone for the Xerox Alto. The Living Computers Museum blog (the museum has closed) became CHM Revolution «Adele Goldberg at Xerox PARC». The CHM C++ archive path became Stroustrup's «A History of C++: 1979–1991». The CHM blog on Cooper became the Gigazine article on Tripod and Visual Basic. Also added CHM «MacPaint and QuickDraw Source Code» and folklore.org «I Still Remember Regions».
erroriFattuali: Atkinson's line from hospital (1982) was embellished: «mi ricordo ancora come si fanno le regioni» instead of «I still remember regions» (folklore.org). Fixed.
Kay's coinage of «object-oriented» was given as certain («Nel 1967») and paraphrased. Kay writes «probably in 1967» and «It's object-oriented programming». Fixed.
Visual Basic «20 maggio 1991»: not confirmable, sources disagree (May 1991 vs 20 March 1991). Softened to May 1991. Fixed.
1968 demo: «ponti radio» and «una cinquantina di chilometri» were not supported (sources speak of leased video links and a home-made modem; the straight-line distance is about 42 km). Fixed.
Xerox Alto attributed to «Thacker con Lampson»: Lampson conceived it (the memo «Why Alto?»), Thacker designed most of it. Fixed.
Before the PARC visit Apple was working on the Lisa as an office computer. The visit is what turned it toward windows and mouse, so «già una macchina con interfaccia grafica» was inaccurate. Fixed.
«Problema per cui gli oggetti sono stati inventati» (graphical interfaces): objects were born for simulation (Simula). Fixed.
Eiffel: «ogni metodo dichiara un contratto» was overstated (contracts are optional). Fixed.
Byte August 1981: «quasi un intero numero» was overstated; it was a special issue. Fixed.
«Inventa il mouse» for Engelbart alone: Bill English built it and is usually named co-inventor. Fixed.
Six sources had URLs that could not be confirmed, or pointed to a closed museum. Replaced.
problemiAperti: WebFetch did not work (DNS error), so the Kay e-mail, folklore.org and Kay's «Early History» were checked only through search snippets and secondary copies. These agree with the wording now used.

Two new source URLs were not checked online: https://www.cl.cam.ac.uk/techreports/UCAM-CL-TR-574.pdf (Sutherland's thesis) and https://www.stroustrup.com/hopl2.pdf (Stroustrup's history of C++). Both are well-known, stable addresses. Gigazine is a secondary source, the only verified account of Tripod I could find.

The 22-search allowance ran out, so these lower-risk facts were checked from knowledge only: the Mac's price and specs ($2.495, 128 KB, 3,5 pollici, 512 × 342), Windows 1.0 (November 1985, tiled windows) and Windows 3.0 (22 May 1990), NeXT adopting Objective-C in 1988, Eiffel 1985–1986, Design Patterns (1994, 23 patterns), Myst made with HyperCard, the birth years of Goldberg (1945), Cooper (1952), Kay (1940) and Stroustrup (1950), Sutherland's Turing Award (1988), and the «rotelle metalliche» in the mouse figure caption.
